description: Solo participant from Colombia with a background in physics and data science. I am building an interactive map for kids aged 8 to 11 that tells the stories of the machines NASA left on the Moon, on Mars and beyond, and the science they made possible. The team is complete and is not looking for new members.
summary: Sentinels of Silence is an interactive story map for children aged 8 to 11 about the machines NASA left on the Moon, on Mars and beyond. The child picks a place, taps a glowing dot and finds the story of a real machine, pinned where NASA says it is: what it was, why it was sent, what it discovered, how it went quiet and where it is today. Seventeen machines are included, from the Apollo 11 landing stage to Pioneer 10. It addresses the challenge by turning technical mission pages into short, accurate stories that connect each piece of hardware with the science it made possible. It matters because children mostly hear about active missions, while the explorers that opened the way are silent and easy to forget.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Sentinels of Silence is a web page with a map of three places: the Moon, Mars and "Beyond" (the rest of the solar system). Each glowing dot is a machine that finished its job and stayed there. Tapping a dot opens its card:

- The story: three short paragraphs written for readers aged 8 to 11.

- What it taught us: the science the machine made possible.

- The plan vs. for real: a bar that compares how long the machine was meant to work with how long it really worked (Opportunity was built for 90 Martian days and lasted almost 15 years).

- How it went quiet, and where it is now.

- Check the facts: links to the NASA pages the card is based on.

A counter ("Found 3 of 17") invites the child to find every machine, and a message celebrates when all 17 have been found.

THE 17 MACHINES

Moon: the Apollo 11 "Eagle" landing stage, the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, the Apollo 12 ALSEP science station and Surveyor 3.

Mars: Viking 1, Viking 2, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, InSight and Ingenuity.

Beyond: the Kepler space telescope, NEAR Shoemaker on asteroid Eros, Dawn in orbit around Ceres, and Pioneer 10 and 11 on their way out of the solar system.

HOW IT WORKS

It is a single static web page written in HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript, with no libraries, no installation and no login, so it opens on a school computer or a phone. The Moon and Mars maps are NASA global mosaics served by NASA Solar System Treks. Each pin is placed from the latitude and longitude published by NASA, converted to a position on the map. The "Beyond" view is a drawing of the solar system and says clearly that it is not to scale.

ACCURACY

Before writing any story, the facts for each machine (dates, landing site, purpose, discoveries, how the mission ended) were collected from NASA pages into one data file, with the source of every entry. The stories use only those facts. Where two NASA pages disagree on the exact day of an event, the card shows only the month, and the data file records the disagreement.

DESIGNED FOR CHILDREN

Short sentences, one idea per sentence, comparisons a child knows, large buttons, and a goal to reach. Every pin is a real button with a text label, the page works with a keyboard, images have descriptions, a list under the map gives the same access as the pins, and the pulsing animation is turned off for people who ask for reduced motion.

BENEFITS AND WHAT I HOPE TO ACHIEVE

A child leaves knowing that these machines are real, where they are, and what each one taught us, and with the idea that a mission does not have to be active to matter. A teacher can use the page in one class with no preparation. Next steps: a Spanish version, a read-aloud voice for each story and a short guide for teachers.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Git and GitHub Pages. Source code: https://github.com/Nicky-AC/spaceappschallenge (folder abandoned_not_forgotten).

NASA Science mission pages, https://science.nasa.gov/ : Surveyor 3, Viking 1, Viking 2, Mars Pathfinder, Mars Exploration Rovers Spirit and Opportunity, Phoenix, InSight, Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer 10, Pioneer 11 and Kepler. Used for the purpose of each mission, its discoveries, how it ended and its images.

3. NASA Solar System Treks, https://trek.nasa.gov/ : base maps of the page. Moon: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter WAC global mosaic (NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University). Mars: Viking MDIM 2.1 colour mosaic (NASA/JPL/USGS). These are the resources listed for the challenge. The exact page behind each fact is listed in data/artifacts.json in the repository and under "Check the facts" on each card.
